cases.name: wide
cases.when: responsive is false, or the container is at least --bp-md -- the default shape, a real <table role="grid">

cases.name: card
cases.when: responsive is true and the container is below --bp-md -- one card per row, no table element at all
cases.reason: Below the breakpoint there is no grid: the rows become stacked cards and nothing renders a table, a row role or a cell. The grid pattern's requirements do not go unmet in this shape, they do not APPLY to it -- there is no grid element for a roving tab stop to live in. A row a consumer made clickable is still reachable by keyboard here, but that is TableRow's own `card-interactive` case bound to `button`, not a clause of this one.

cases.name: empty
cases.when: no TableRow is written -- the [empty] slot alone, with no grid drawn at all
cases.reason: There is no grid in this shape, so the grid pattern's requirements do not go unmet, they do not APPLY. A role="grid" holding neither a header row nor a data row is a degenerate render, the same judgement Tabs makes when it draws no tabpanel for a tab that does not exist, and a column head standing over a "no results" sentence describes a table that is not there. The measurement that settled it: across sixteen tables in a real consumer the slot had zero uses and was replaced every time by an @if that removed the table entirely.
